---
title: "R Setup"
subtitle: "Installing the tools the companion pages use"
---

## You don't need this to follow the lectures

Every chapter slide deck is self-contained. You can watch the entire course and never touch R. The R code on the companion pages is there to *read* first; running it is optional, and only needed if you want to try the exercises hands-on.

If you do want to run the code yourself, this page tells you what to install.

## What you will need

| Tool | Purpose | Where to get it |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| **R 4.3+** | The programming language | [r-project.org](https://www.r-project.org/) |
| **RStudio** | A friendly editor for R | [posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) |
| **Quarto 1.8+** | (optional) for re-rendering the slide decks yourself | [quarto.org](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) |

Install in that order. R first. RStudio second. Quarto third.

## The R packages used in this course

Open RStudio. In the **console** at the bottom, paste this line and press Enter:

```r
install.packages(c("dagitty", "ggdag", "bnlearn", "ggplot2",
                   "tidyr", "dplyr", "tibble", "gRain"))
```

That installs everything the companion pages need. The first install can take a few minutes — be patient.

## What each package does

| Package | What it does | Used in |
|---------|--------------|---------|
| **dagitty** | Builds and queries causal diagrams | Ch 1, 2, 3, 6 |
| **ggdag** | Draws dagitty diagrams nicely | Ch 1, 2, 3, 6 |
| **bnlearn** | Builds Bayesian networks (pictures with lookup tables) | Ch 4, 5, 10 |
| **gRain** | Asks Bayesian networks specific questions | Ch 4, 5 |
| **ggplot2** | Makes histograms and plots | Ch 8 |
| **dplyr / tidyr / tibble** | Data manipulation helpers | Ch 6, 7, 8, 9 |

## Verifying the install

Paste this into the RStudio console. If every line returns a version number without an error, you are set:

```r
packageVersion("dagitty")
packageVersion("ggdag")
packageVersion("bnlearn")
packageVersion("gRain")
packageVersion("ggplot2")
packageVersion("dplyr")
```

## Common installation problems

### `bnlearn` fails to install on Windows

You may need [**Rtools**](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/), which provides the compiler `bnlearn` needs on Windows. Install Rtools, restart RStudio, then re-run the install.packages line.

### `gRain` complains about Bioconductor dependencies

`gRain` depends on a package called `graph` from Bioconductor. Install it with:

```r
if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(c("graph", "RBGL"))
```

Then re-run the install.packages line.

### Older R version

The course is tested against R 4.3 and later. If you are on R 4.2 or earlier, please update — several of the packages above will fail or behave unexpectedly on older versions.

## Don't have time to install anything?

You can read every R workshop on the companion pages without running it. The code is annotated line-by-line, and the explanatory paragraphs around each block tell you what the code does and what to expect from the output. Reading is enough to get the ideas; running is for when you are ready to try them on your own data.
